name: billy woods
label: Backwoodz Studioz
lede: billy woods, born in D.C. and raised in Zimbabwe, keeps his face out of the pictures, runs his own label, and spent two decades in New York's underground before Pitchfork ranked GOLLIWOG No. 21 of 2025.

eras.title: A front-row seat, then a laundromat
eras.text: Born in Washington, D.C., raised for nearly a decade in newly independent Zimbabwe, back in the States at eleven. The rapper who will later hide his face arrives with a Jamaican mother, a Zimbabwean father and a head full of Public Enemy.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · UGSMAG: billy woods · Bandcamp Daily: Billy Woods Raps From the Shadows
years.h: woods is born in D.C., one parent Jamaican, the other Zimbabwean
years.p: [[billy woods|f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba]]'s mother is a Jamaican English-literature professor. His father is a Zimbabwean Marxist intellectual, in the U.S. finishing a Ph.D. while the war for Zimbabwe's independence plays out.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the birth around 1978. He has never made his birth name public and keeps his face out of photos; in 2013 the interviewer MC Eleven, who had known him since 2008, admitted he still had no clear idea what woods looks like. Per Wikipedia, woods told Jacobin the anonymity comes from wanting privacy and no association with his family name.

Bandcamp Daily describes the father as an activist and writer for Zimbabwean independence while exiled in America. "My dad was a writer and an intellectual. He wasn't a fighter," woods says there. In 1980 the family moved to Zimbabwe and his father joined the new government, giving woods a front-row seat to a country working out its future. His father died in the 1980s; woods and his mother left for the U.S. about eighteen months later.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Bandcamp Daily: Billy Woods Raps From the Shadows
years.h: Back in the U.S. at eleven, he gets into Public Enemy
years.p: After his father's death, woods and his mother return to the States. Spike Lee's Do the Right Thing and [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]] are how hip-hop gets in.
years.xp:
"It was 1989 or so, and I distinctly remember getting into Public Enemy," he tells Bandcamp Daily. He calls himself "this rebellious, anti-authoritarian kid."

He later attends Howard University for a stretch, then a small liberal arts college in the Northeast, before heading for New York.

years.src: Okayplayer: 'The Music Industry Was Detonating Underneath Us · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: He meets Vordul Mega at nineteen and starts writing
years.p: In D.C., woods meets [[Vordul Mega|787c9240-273a-42b3-9163-3ece4c865d71]] of [[Cannibal Ox|38411d0a-5636-46ba-befb-67cca6f4b9c7]]. The next year, in a laundromat in Kennebunk, Maine, he writes what he calls his first real rhyme.
years.xp:
"I met Vordul in 1996, or so, and wasn't rapping or anything like that," woods tells Okayplayer. He remembers being the only person in D.C. playing Cannibal Ox, and Vordul telling him in 1999 that El-P had signed the group; he was not totally sure he believed it. Hearing early versions of tracks like "Pigeons" hit him hard.

His own tally of what the group sold: "Cannibal Ox did like 80,000 units or some shit."

eras.title: Wrong decade to start a record label
eras.text: New York, a one-man label and a rap underground that had moved on to Dipset. woods releases anyway, alone and in crews, for a decade that pays nothing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Backwoodz Studioz · Wikipedia: Vordul Mega · Bandcamp Daily: Billy Woods Raps From the Shadows · Okayplayer: 'The Music Industry Was Detonating Underneath Us
years.h: Camouflage: a one-man label's first solo record
years.p: Built on production from 007 (Bond), with [[Vordul Mega|787c9240-273a-42b3-9163-3ece4c865d71]] on about a third of it, Camouflage is later filed as woods's solo debut. It comes out through his own new Backwoodz Studioz.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says he founded Backwoodz in 2002 as a one-man operation, inspired by indie successes like The Cold Vein and Operation: Doomsday, and rented studio time from Anton Schlesinger, then a Caroline Records intern and later the label's president. Bandcamp Daily says 2003, and sources split on whether Camouflage is 2002 or 2003.

He moved to New York for good in 2001: "If I just sit around here depressed, hanging out with these dudes, I'm gonna be here forever." On the label: "I was an outsider in a crowded scene, and nobody liked my shit!" And to Okayplayer: "It wasn't a great era for me to start a record label in, however." The same people praising Aesop Rock, he says, were suddenly "only listening to Dipset."

years.src: Wikipedia: Vordul Mega · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Terror Firma puts ten New York rappers on one Backwoodz album
years.p: woods joins [[Vordul Mega|787c9240-273a-42b3-9163-3ece4c865d71]], Akir and others from a spread of crews for the Reavers' Terror Firma. Some critics liked the grit; others never warmed to it.
years.xp: The notices come from Wikipedia's Vordul Mega page, which says some praised the record's grit and creativity and others did not warm to it.

years.src: Okayplayer: 'The Music Industry Was Detonating Underneath Us · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: With Privilege, woods makes three albums as Super Chron Flight Brothers
years.p: Emergency Powers: The World Tour (2007), Indonesia (2009) and Cape Verde (2010). The duo splits in the early 2010s.
years.xp: woods tells Okayplayer this was the comedy-and-tragedy stretch of his output, and that by 2007 the indie-rap market that had been fertile in 2003 "was no longer fertile ground." He tells UGSMAG the Privilege partnership "was like family for me." HipHopDX reviewed Cape Verde in August 2010, and Wikipedia says Backwoodz was struggling financially by the time the duo ended.

eras.title: The album that was supposed to be the last one
eras.text: With the label short of money and the group gone, woods plans an exit. The record he means as a goodbye turns him from a cult name into the center of a scene, and he meets the partner who defines the next decade.

years.big: If HWAM flops, the label is done.
years.src: Bandcamp Daily: Backwoodz Studioz · Wikipedia: History Will Absolve Me · UGSMAG: billy woods
years.h: He plans History Will Absolve Me as his way out
years.p: woods tells Bandcamp Daily that was his thinking going in, with Super Chron Flight Brothers over and Backwoodz short of money: he says he was not sure he would have quit rapping, but was kind of prepared to.
years.xp:
It did the opposite. The cover is a photo of Zimbabwean revolutionary Robert Mugabe and the title comes from a Fidel Castro speech. Wikipedia calls it a cult classic of underground hip-hop, Pitchfork later named it the turning point for woods and the label, and it was Backwoodz's first release sold directly to fans through its own website.

Exclaim! reviewed it in April 2012. UGSMAG has woods naming "The Man Who Would Be King" and "The Wake" as songs where he finally grasped what he had been chasing for years, and crediting producers Bond, Marmaduke, Willie Green and A.M. Breakups.

years.cap: billy woods and Elucid, Armand Hammer live, October 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Armand Hammer (group) · Wikipedia: Backwoodz Studioz
years.h: Uncommon Nasa introduces him to Elucid
years.p: woods and [[Elucid|1206c904-9282-494d-b9c7-49e8fb201e69]] form [[Armand Hammer|167a6f86-2c26-43fe-82f0-e4c8a39ea490]], named after the industrialist, and release the mixtape Half Measures and the album Race Music.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the two met through the New York rapper Uncommon Nasa, and Elucid signed to Backwoodz around this time. He appears on History Will Absolve Me. Stephen Weil later called Race Music a potent record about life, art, sex, drugs, politics and violence.

years.cap: billy woods and Elucid, Armand Hammer live, December 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Bandcamp Daily: Backwoodz Studioz
years.h: Blockhead beats, start to finish, on Dour Candy
years.p: Pitchfork's Nate Patrin reviewed it that August; Noisey's Zachary Lipez called it an invigorating hangover.
years.xp: woods tells UGSMAG it is "my first one producer, one rapper album," and that the lead single is "one of the best songs I ever did." Blockhead, real name Tony Simon, later released his own Funeral Balloons on Backwoodz.

eras.title: Armand Hammer becomes a name you drop
eras.text: Rome, Paraffin, Hiding Places and Shrines arrive in four years, and the reviews start repeating themselves. The producer list gets longer, the writing gets denser, and Backwoodz becomes a destination.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: The Village Voice says Chekhov would listen to him
years.p: Rolling Stone puts Known Unknowns on a list of 15 great albums you did not hear.
years.xp: The Voice headline reads, in full, "Billy Woods Is The Underground Rapper Chekhov Would Listen To." Noisey followed in October with a profile arguing woods stands "at the forefront of rap's avant-garde."

years.cap: billy woods and Elucid, Armand Hammer live, August 2014
years.src: Wikipedia: Rome (Armand Hammer album)
years.h: Rome takes Armand Hammer further into the dark
years.p: Messiah Musik, August Fanon, High Priest, Kenny Segal and JPEGMafia are among the producers. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: Phillip Mlynar wrote that the duo had burrowed deeper into the leftfield, moving on from boom-bap theology. Paul Thompson at Vulture called it their best. In 2025 Pitchfork placed it at No. 73 on its list of the 100 best rap albums of all time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paraffin (album)
years.h: Paraffin goes to vinyl first
years.p: Backwoodz presses Armand Hammer's third album before the digital, cassette and CD editions. Pitchfork's Paul A. Thompson hears it attuned to the political, physical and ethical realities of 2018.
years.xp: Stereogum ranked it fourth among its best rap albums of 2018. It also landed on year-end lists at Pitchfork, the A.V. Club, Bandcamp Daily (No. 28) and PopMatters (No. 65).

years.cap: The William Livingstone House, Detroit, photographed in 2006 by Yves Marchand and Romain Meffre
years.src: Wikipedia: Hiding Places · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Hiding Places hands Kenny Segal the whole record
years.p: The Los Angeles producer had already made beats for Armand Hammer's Rome and Paraffin. Pitchfork gave the album 7.7.
years.xp:
Segal came into woods's orbit through Milo's So the Flies Don't Come, which featured Elucid. Pitchfork's Marcus J. Moore heard early-2000s New York underground rap in it and an edginess like Cannibal Ox's The Cold Vein; the Fader called it woods's leanest and best.

It showed up on year-end lists at Time (No. 5), NPR (No. 9), Stereogum (No. 9) and Vice (No. 8). woods also released the solo Terror Management that year, and NPR's Rodney Carmichael put it on a list of Afro-dystopian rap albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shrines (Armand Hammer album)
years.h: "Bitter Cassava" starts in Edinburgh and ends up on Shrines
years.p: woods begins it on a 2019 European tour and finishes it in New York. Guests across the album include Earl Sweatshirt, Moor Mother, Pink Siifu and Quelle Chris.
years.xp: Producers include Earl Sweatshirt, Navy Blue, Nicholas Craven, Child Actor, Andrew Broder and Kenny Segal, with Willie Green as co-executive producer. Pitchfork gave it 8.0; the Quietus's Eden Tizard heard a new clarity after the monolithic Paraffin.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Wikipedia: Shrines (Armand Hammer album)
years.h: Brass pairs him with the Philadelphia poet Moor Mother
years.p: Wikipedia's timeline lists the collaborative album as a 2020 release. [[Moor Mother|16610cf1-5ed5-4770-89b4-bf7e7aca7ebf]] also appears on Armand Hammer's Shrines and We Buy Diabetic Test Strips.

eras.title: The Alchemist, two solo albums, Fat Possum
eras.text: The Alchemist produces a full Armand Hammer album, woods releases two solo records in 2022, and Backwoodz signs a distribution deal with Fat Possum.

years.src: Wikipedia: Haram (album) · Wikipedia: billy woods
yt: 'Falling Out the Sky' with Earl Sweatshirt, official video
years.h: The Alchemist produces every track on Haram
years.p: Earl Sweatshirt co-produces one track and guests, with Quelle Chris and Curly Castro.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and later ranked it No. 26 among 2021's best albums. The cover, showing decapitated pigs, drew a PETA statement calling it terrifying and urging people to focus on the music instead.

The Washington Post's Zachary Lipez wrote in March 2021 that the Alchemist made for an even more intriguing brand of underground rap.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aethiopes (album)
yt: 'Spongebob' live at The Loft, with Armand Hammer
years.h: Preservation produces every track on Aethiopes
years.p: The cover borrows Rembrandt's 1661 Two Moors, and the title is an old European word for African peoples. Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp: It topped Treble's year-end list and hit No. 2 at Gorilla vs. Bear, No. 3 at the Ringer and No. 5 at Stereogum. A U.S. tour ran May to October and included Le Guess Who? in the Netherlands in November.

years.src: Wikipedia: Church (billy woods album)
years.h: Church follows Aethiopes within six months
years.p: The second solo record of 2022 is produced almost entirely by Messiah Musik, with Elucid, Akai Solo, Fielded and Fat Ray guesting.
years.xp: woods said the album's launching point was cannabis he had not encountered in years, which grew into a record about a certain era in New York, then faith and belief. Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and BrooklynVegan put it at No. 26 for the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Backwoodz Studioz · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Pitchfork's Dylan Green profiles Backwoodz
years.p: The feature traces how the label built its run in New York indie rap; a Fat Possum distribution deal follows.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Fat Possum deal to 2023, with Anton Schlesinger as president and woods on A&R and executive production. That year woods also published the children's book A is for Anarchist with the illustrator M. Musgrove (Rizzoli Universe). Armand Hammer's We Buy Diabetic Test Strips came out that September on Fat Possum, their first album outside Backwoodz.

years.src: Wikipedia: Maps (Billy Woods and Kenny Segal album) · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Seventy percent of Maps gets written on tour
years.p: A travelogue with Kenny Segal, featuring Danny Brown, Aesop Rock, Quelle Chris, Benjamin Booker and Samuel T. Herring. Pitchfork gave it 8.9.
years.xp:
Written mostly on the road after pandemic restrictions eased and recorded partly in Los Angeles, it is lighter than Hiding Places. Metacritic gave it 90. Pitchfork and Stereogum both ranked it No. 3 of 2023.

NPR's Sheldon Pearce called it a master class, even for one of rap's greatest-ever penmen. Rolling Stone's Mosi Reeves headlined his review with a warning that it is designed to get you lost.

years.src: Wikipedia: We Buy Diabetic Test Strips
years.h: We Buy Diabetic Test Strips takes Armand Hammer to Fat Possum
years.p: El-P, JPEGMAFIA and Kenny Segal are among the producers, with Shabaka Hutchings and Child Actor in the sessions. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.1; Metacritic scored it 87. BrooklynVegan ranked it No. 2 for the year, Vulture No. 6 and the Ringer No. 7. Guests include JPEGMAFIA, Moor Mother, El-P, Pink Siifu and Soul Glo's Pierce Jordan.

eras.title: GOLLIWOG
eras.text: The most confrontational record of woods's career brings the biggest reviews of it. The cover is a golliwog doll, sixteen producers are on the tracklist, and the year ends with him on a Pitchfork best-of list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Golliwog (album)
years.h: "Misery" announces GOLLIWOG, with Kenny Segal on the beat
years.p: Two minutes of Segal. "Blk Zmby" follows April 11, and "Lead Paint Test," with Elucid and Cavalier, on May 7.
years.xp: The rollout included a Knockdown Center show in New York. Wikipedia counts it as woods's ninth solo studio album, released again on Backwoodz.

years.src: Wikipedia: Golliwog (album) · Album of the Year: billy woods, GOLLIWOG · Pitchfork: billy woods, GOLLIWOG
years.h: Pitchfork gives GOLLIWOG 8.7 and ranks it No. 21 of 2025
years.p: Eighteen tracks in 52 minutes, with the Alchemist, El-P, Ant, Conductor Williams, Shabaka Hutchings, DJ Haram, Willie Green and more producing. The cover is a golliwog doll.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's review is by Stephen Kearse (May 12). Wikipedia reports a Metacritic score of 88, with 9/10 from Clash, Exclaim! and the Line of Best Fit; Album of the Year quotes Pitchfork calling it a twisty horrorcore masterpiece where history and nightmares are indistinguishable. The Guardian found "moments of beauty amid the bleakness."

Guests are Elucid (three tracks), Despot, Bruiser Wolf, al.divino, Cavalier and Yolanda Watson. Willie Green mastered all of it and mixed 14 songs. In the UK it reached No. 7 on the R&B chart and No. 26 on the independent chart, and No. 41 in Germany.

years.big: Billy Woods Is Scary Good at Rapping
years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Wikipedia: Golliwog (album)
years.h: The Times profiles woods six days after GOLLIWOG drops
years.p: That is the New York Times's own headline, over a profile of a rapper who keeps his face out of publicity photos.
years.xp: The reviews leaned on the same idea from the other side: Clash called the record "abrasive, demanding," and Slant called it "intensely confrontational" and unwilling to "hold your hand."

years.src: Wikipedia: Mercy (Armand Hammer and the Alchemist album)
years.h: The Alchemist and Armand Hammer do it again on Mercy
years.p: Announced September 10, with Earl Sweatshirt, Quelle Chris and Pink Siifu. Pitchfork's Dash Lewis gave it 8.0.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Dash Lewis gave it 8.0 and called some of the Alchemist's production his weirdest and most harrowing since The Skeleton Key. Paste ranked it seventh among the best rap albums of 2025.

years.src: Album of the Year: billy woods, GOLLIWOG · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Treble puts GOLLIWOG first on its year-end list
years.p: The Wire has it at No. 2 and Rolling Stone's Rob Sheffield at No. 4, per Album of the Year; Pitchfork lands it at No. 21.
years.xp: Album of the Year has it as the sixth-best-reviewed album of 2025 by its critic average, scored 87 from 21 reviews.
